chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskān, from Yazīd ibn Farqad, who said:
I said to Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him): 'Is the Sadaqat al-Fitr (Zakat al-Fitr) obligatory for the needy person?' He said, 'No.'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū 'Abdillāh, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْمُحْتَاجِ: The needy person, one who has sufficient food for the day but not surplus
key_terms.صَدَقَةُ الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (Sadaqat al-Fitr), the charity given at the end of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: Is Zakat al-Fitr obligatory for the poor and needy in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) confirms that the *muḥtāj* (one who possesses basic necessities but lacks surplus) is exempt from paying Zakat al-Fitr, distinguishing them from the *faqir* (poor) who may receive it. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that Zakat al-Fitr is a duty for those with surplus wealth, reinforcing the principle that the needy are primarily recipients rather than payers of this specific charity.
